test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means 'A is the brother of B',

A - B means 'A is the wife of B',

A × B means 'A is the father of B',

and A ÷ B means 'A is the sister of B'.

How is P related to T if 'P × Q ÷ R - S × T'?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47a89a5bb9daa01f32d67cf5151f1acc95989e845ae3c3eb86353e0d1da9cbdc.png] 

Decoding the Symbols:

 
 

 Symbol
 +
 -
 ×
 ÷
 
 

 Meaning
 Brother
 Wife 
 Father 
 Sister 
 
 

 

Given: P × Q ÷ R - S × T

It means: P is the father of Q, Q is the sister of R, R is the wife of S and S is the father of T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e2363490b5145e9d8196b16038968069ee2fd17797d8ef42ad99eef9cd28982.png] 

So, P is the '**Mother's father**' of T.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
